title: An overview of SwiftTesting and XCUITest on iOS

videos.script: Many of the phones your users hold are not Android. They are iPhones, and an iPhone app is tested with Apple's own tools. {{iphone}} Those tools run on a Mac, and only there. Xcode, the simulator and the UI tests all live on macOS. {{wall}} This course has no Mac, so this lesson shows the code and does not run it. It says so wherever that matters. {{honest}} Apple gives you two frameworks. Swift Testing checks the code behind the screens, such as how a price is written. It is the newer of the two. {{swift-testing}} XCUITest drives the app itself. It launches it from a second program and taps it from outside, the way Appium does. {{xcuitest}} You will read a test of each, written for an iOS version of Tickets. Then how they are run, in Xcode and on the command line. {{run}} And last, Espresso, XCUITest and Appium side by side, so you can say which one a team should use, and why. {{compare}}
